_comment: Expansion 2.0: The Neural Court (src/engine/neural_engine.py). Courtiers speak through a LOCAL language model
served by Ollama (https://ollama.com) on the player's own machine: no cloud, no API key, no cost.
host must be a loopback address (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1): the game never sends the campaign anywhere else.
Override for one run with the environment variable CT_OLLAMA_HOST; CT_NEURAL=off disables the feature.
model: any chat model pulled with `ollama pull <model>`. The ping checks it is installed.
ping_timeout: seconds to wait for Ollama to answer the availability check (the game never hangs on it).
The answer is cached for ping_cache_seconds.
chat_timeout: seconds to wait for a reply before giving up and using the scripted fallback.
loyalty_change: the model's verdict on each exchange is clamped to [min, max]; weekly_loyalty_cap caps the total
any one courtier can gain or lose from conversation in a single week (no farming loyalty by chatting).
memory_exchanges: how many past exchanges with a courtier are replayed to the model (and kept in the save).
max_player_chars: the longest line the Lord Protector may speak.
fallback: scripted replies (by the courtier's loyalty band) used when Ollama is not running. PLACEHOLDERS for the
tone: Speak in a gritty, clipped 1980s Cold-War bureaucratic tone.

loyal: {name} bows. 'As you command, Lord Protector. My office stands ready.'
'The House endures, {ruler}. Tell me what you need and it will be done.'
wary: {name} studies you for a long moment. 'I hear you, Lord Protector. We shall see.'
'Your words are noted, {ruler}. The Chamberlain will minute them.'
hostile: {name} does not quite meet your eye. 'Of course, Lord Protector. Whatever you say.'
A thin smile. 'The {role} has many duties, {ruler}. I shall attend to them.'
